rationale: All three blocking findings from the final round are resolved by the fix-up diff, each with direct test coverage. CR-001: App.tsx now gates SkipLink behind `user && isConfigFetched`, verified by a new App.test.tsx with 3 tests covering the loading window, authenticated-but-config-not-fetched window, and the authenticated+config-fetched render. CR-002: SkipLink.tsx adds an onClick handler (preventDefault + explicit document.getElementById('main-content')?.focus()) giving cross-browser focus-shift robustness independent of native hash-navigation behavior, verified by a new jsdom-executable test asserting the target gains focus on click. CR-003: all `focus:` classes were switched to `focus-visible:`, verified by the updated 'is visually hidden until keyboard-focused' test. The fix-up diff is scoped entirely to these three concerns (a conditional render guard, a DOM focus call, and a Tailwind class-prefix rename) and introduces no new security, public-API, data-loss, or build/runtime risk, so no confirmation pass was needed.

finding_status.notes: src/App.tsx:68 now renders `{user && isConfigFetched && <SkipLink />}` instead of an unconditional `<SkipLink />`, so the link never exists while its #main-content target is absent from the DOM. New src/__tests__/App.test.tsx covers both the no-user and authenticated-but-not-configured windows (skip link absent) and the fully-loaded window (skip link present).

src/components/SkipLink/SkipLink.tsx adds `onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); document.getElementById('main-content')?.focus() }}`, giving an explicit, browser-independent focus-shift path that doesn't rely on native hash-navigation-plus-tabindex behavior. The new SkipLink test ('moves focus to the main content landmark on click') exercises this directly in jsdom by rendering a sibling `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} />`, clicking the link, and asserting the main element has focus.

All `focus:` class prefixes in SkipLink.tsx's className were replaced with `focus-visible:` (not-sr-only, absolute, top-4, left-4, z-50, rounded, bg-surface-base-primary, px-4, py-2, text-text-primary, outline-none, ring-2, ring-border-accent), so the link only becomes visible on keyboard-driven focus. The renamed test 'is visually hidden until keyboard-focused' now asserts the `focus-visible:not-sr-only` class.
